description: Deployed by the IT department where developers cannot write (ProgramData, /Library/Application Support, /etc).

contact.description: Who to ask for an exception (e-mail, URL).

enforce.description: Settings imposed on every repository; developers cannot override them.

areas.description: Names of area/ labels, usually the commit scopes.

managedBy.description: Tool already managing this repository (opentofu, terraform…): ship sync then only reports differences.

dateField.description: Date field that receives the milestone's due date, such as "Target date" (for the Roadmap view). Empty: off.

done.description: Status of a closed roadmap issue.

inProgress.description: Status ship publish sets when it opens a pull request that closes an issue of the project.

phaseField.description: Single-select field that receives the milestone's title, such as "Phase"; its options must exist (the REST API cannot add them). Empty: off.

statusField.description: Single-select field holding the status. Empty: the status is left alone.

todo.description: Status of an open roadmap issue that has none yet (a status set by hand is kept).

url.description: GitHub Project (v2) to keep up to date: its URL (https://github.com/orgs/acme/projects/7, https://github.com/users/ada/projects/3) or owner/number (acme/7). Empty: no project. The token needs the project scope (gh auth refresh -s project).

issue.description: "first" starts the branch description with the issue number or tracker ticket (feat/42-add-login), "none" leaves it out.

maxLength.description: Longest description part of a branch name, after the prefix and the issue number.

maxWords.description: Words kept from the subject in a branch name (stop words such as "the" are dropped first).

bodyWidth.description: Column at which commit bodies (the why) are wrapped.

gitmoji.description: Where the gitmoji goes: "auto" follows the repository's last 50 commits (ship-it's "first" when fewer than 5 are conventional), "first" (✨ feat: x), "after-type" (feat: ✨ x) or "none" (feat: x).

headerMaxLength.description: Longest title, gitmoji included (✨ feat(scope): subject). The planner drops the scope of a longer one.

scopeFrom.description: Where the planner takes the scope from: "folders", the deepest folder the changed files share, or "none" (you write it).

scopeRequired.description: Refuse a title without a scope.

scopes.description: Scopes a title may use; empty: any scope. The planner drops a scope that is not listed.

sign.description: Sign commits: "auto" follows git's commit.gpgSign, "always" signs (git commit -S) and refuses to commit without a signing key (user.signingKey), "never" does not sign (--no-gpg-sign). Rebases and merges made before a publication follow it too.

signoff.description: Add a Signed-off-by trailer (DCO) with the committer's identity, as git commit -s does. "auto": when the repository asks for it, that is when most of its last 50 commits carry one, its CONTRIBUTING file mentions the DCO or Signed-off-by, or it configures the DCO app (.github/dco.yml).

subjectMaxLength.description: Longest subject, in characters (after "type(scope): "; a tracker ticket at the end does not count).

branchPrefix.description: Conventional Branch prefix of its branches, such as feat or chore.

emoji.description: Gitmoji of the type, written in titles.

label.description: Kind of its pull requests, after "kind/"; "" for none.

release.description: Version increment of its commits: major, minor, patch or none (built-in: feat minor; fix, perf, security and revert patch; the others none). A breaking change is always major.

types.description: Changes to the built-in commit types, by type: {"emoji", "branchPrefix", "label", "release"} changes a type or adds one (a new type needs an emoji and a branch prefix), false removes a built-in type. label is the kind/ label of its pull requests ("": none); release its version increment (major, minor, patch or none; a breaking change is always major). ship types lists the result.

allowSkip.description: Accept --skip-gates (troubleshooting). false: the checks always run before a push.

beforeCommit.description: Also run the checks before the commit of ship and ship_deliver: a red check refuses the commit. Off by default, so that a commit stays instant and the checks run once, before the push.

enabled.description: Run the project's own checks for each ecosystem it uses (the package.json scripts lint, typecheck and test; gofmt, go vet and go test; cargo fmt, clippy and test; and so on for Python, PHP, Ruby, JVM and .NET) before every push. ship check gates runs them on demand, and beforeCommit before the commit too. false: no check runs.

remote.description: Remote ship fetches from and pushes to, and whose GitHub repository it works with. In a fork, pull requests still open on the parent repository.

keyword.description: Keyword linking the issue in the pull request body.

trackerKeys.description: Project keys of an external tracker (Jira, Linear), such as ACME: a ticket ACME-123 in the branch name ends the commit and pull request titles, "(ACME-123)", and the branch keeps it in upper case.

blackBoxBytes.description: Size in bytes of the in-memory black box (DEBUG records of the run), written to disk only when a run fails. At least 64 KiB.

keepRuns.description: Number of past runs whose journal is kept in each log directory (.git/ship/logs, or the user log directory).

maxBytes.description: Total size in bytes kept in each log directory; the oldest runs go first. At least 1 MiB.

mode.description: Whether ship pushes and opens the pull request after committing: "auto", or "never" (as --local; ship publish publishes later).

overlaps.description: Before pushing, and in ship status, warn about the open pull requests into the same base that change the same or adjacent lines as the branch: a likely conflict for whoever merges second. It never stops a publication.

update.description: How a branch behind its base is brought up to date before publishing: "rebase" replays it on the base (the push then uses a lease), "merge" merges the base into it (no rewrite, a normal push), "none" publishes it as it is. A checkpoint comes first; on a conflict ship cancels and publishes as it is.

assignSelf.description: Assign a new pull request to its author.

base.description: Base branch of new pull requests, and the branch ship brings a branch up to date with; empty: the default branch of the repository on GitHub (of the parent repository, in a fork). Closing keywords only work on the default branch: on another base, the issue is linked with Refs.

draft.description: When a new pull request is a draft: "unattended" when nobody reviewed the plan in a terminal (--yes), "always", or "never". Work in progress commits, ship publish --draft and AI agents always open a draft.

kind.description: Prefix of the kind labels: kind/feature, kind/bug… The commit types name the kinds (ship.commits.types.<type>.label).

size.description: Prefix of the size labels: size/XS… (ship.pullRequest.sizes).

labels.description: Add the kind and size labels the repository already has.

maxLines.description: Changed lines (generated files excluded) above which the plan warns and suggests a split. Reviews lose effectiveness beyond about 400.

milestone.description: "issue" puts a new pull request in the milestone of the issue it closes, "none" leaves milestones alone.

reviewers.description: Logins whose review is requested on a new pull request (never its author). A request GitHub refuses is a warning.

changes.description: Sum up the diff in the pull request body: the files added, changed, renamed and removed, and the declarations added and removed.

issue.description: Link the issue (Closes #12) in ship's own pull request body.

testing.description: Write the Testing section (the checks that passed locally, the Tested: notes) in ship's own pull request body.

why.description: Write the why of the commits (their bodies) in ship's own pull request body.

sizes.description: Size labels, by name (after the size prefix), and the number of changed lines, generated files excluded, under which each applies; 0 marks the size of everything larger. The default is Kubernetes' scale.

teamReviewers.description: Teams of the repository's organisation, by slug, whose review is requested on a new pull request. A request GitHub refuses is a warning.

template.description: Pull request body: "auto" fills the repository's pull request template when it has one (as GitHub finds it on the default branch), "ship" always uses ship-it's format, or the path of a template in the repository (for a .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/ directory).

allow.description: Findings accepted, by the fingerprint ship prints with each one (PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 of the value, salted with the rule id), never by value: a value in a file would leak it.

disabledRules.description: Built-in rules turned off, by id.

ignorePaths.description: Glob patterns of files never scanned for secrets (false positives); dir/** for a whole directory.

rules.description: Extra rules: an id, a Go regular expression (RE2) and the literal keywords a line must contain for the pattern to run (compared without case when the pattern has (?i)). The value reported is the first capture group, else the whole match.

id.description: Name shown with each finding; not the id of a built-in rule.

keywords.description: Literals a line must contain, one at least, for the pattern to run: they keep the scan fast.

pattern.description: Go regular expression (RE2) matched against each added line; (?i) ignores case. It must not match an empty text.

maxLayers.description: Most layers ship stack splits the work into; the smaller areas are grouped in the top layer beyond it.

rebase.description: Who rebases the layers above a merged one: "github" (GitHub's own rebase, which creates signed replacement commits; ship stack sync only follows it) or "local" (ship stack sync rebases on this machine with your signing key, then pushes with a lease). A classic chain of pull requests is always rebased locally.

auto.description: Run ship tidy at the start of ship: leave a branch whose pull request was merged for the updated base, with the work in progress. ship tidy itself always runs.

deleteMerged.description: Delete the local branches whose pull request was merged and that hold nothing more (ship undo recreates them).

accessible.description: Plain interface for screen readers: no full-screen review, one question per line, as --plain and SHIP_ACCESSIBLE=1.

color.description: Colours of the review screen: "auto" follows the terminal, "always" keeps them when the terminal is not detected as colour-capable, "never" removes them. NO_COLOR, when set, always wins.

language.description: Language of messages: "auto" reads SHIP_LANG, then the locale (LC_ALL, LC_MESSAGES, LANG). SHIP_LANG, when set, wins over this setting.

reviewScreen.description: Show the review screen of ship in a terminal; false asks one confirmation instead (the plan is printed first).

organization.description: Name shown to developers when a setting is imposed.

title: ship-it organisation policy
